The a91f0807 image reproduced a permanent File-I/O runtime orphan: git help emitted repeated execve EIO and later ls/stat emitted repeated newfstatat EIO. Commit 3d6b65223 requeues a live PageContainer claim with the same registry and wake source and makes AP/BSP convergence resubmit it. The fixed physical image passed write, stat, read, chmod, exec, and git help on the same MMC direct-root RW path.

The physically booted fixed image is /srv/tftp/txv2/vf2-accept-3d6b6522-ea831da8-20260816-041139-cst/txv2-vf2-3d6b6522-ea831da8.uimage, 5,362,144 bytes, SHA-256 ea831da84c8a7ad220805618374f3fb4728af4c360619b5b2d893a472e5dbf43. Host cmp and mkimage inspection passed; every U-Boot transfer reported 5,362,144 bytes and iminfo checksum OK.

Formal Git baseline init, repository-local name/email, README creation, and git add completed. git commit did not return a summary or shell prompt. A later same-image, same-MMC RO boot proved commit b574dba3b66bdd0e4cb2a3327ea2f5163b3752e3, the matching master ref and log, clean git status, and git fsck --full exit 0. The commit is durable, but the command-completion requirement failed.

A qemu-riscv64 syscall replay of the same Git 2.49.1 showed refs are published before git maintenance run --auto --no-quiet --detach and a parent wait4. This makes post-commit process lifecycle the leading hypothesis, but the hung physical run had no valid stall snapshot, so wait4 is not claimed as the sole proven root cause.

Commit f11ad1076 fixes a separate proven wait interruption bug: ProcessIdentity now delegates thread_signal_interrupts_wait to the existing disposition-aware pending-signal predicate. This explains why a wait could consume SIGINT or SIGCANCEL and park again; the previously failing focused drive test and the full 24-test drive integration suite pass. This source change has not been built or physically booted because the MMC RW blocker appeared first.

After the hung commit was physically reset, the same fixed image with tx.root=mmcblk0 rw failed at mount:rootfs:ext4:mmcblk0:stage=rw-discovered:errno=EIO, fell back to tmpfs, and panicked when /bin/sh was absent. The aggregate RW path can include journal replay, home-block writes, barriers, orphan recovery, recovery-bit writes, and runtime construction, so the sentinel does not prove zero device writes before failure.

The same MMC still mounts and reads successfully with tx.root=mmcblk0 ro. README and recovery-probe hashes, Git HEAD/log/status, and git fsck are readable. The hard boundary forbids repair fsck, raw writes, or blind RW retries, so Vim, GCC, Rust, full non-shallow clone, the final synced reset, and complete RO durability verification remain unexecuted and failed as a matrix. Do not invite push or pull verification.

rw-discovered:EIO is an aggregate mount failure. The RW path may attempt journal replay/home-block writes, barriers, orphan recovery, recovery-bit writes, and runtime construction before returning EIO; never report it as a guaranteed no-write failure.

A final-ro tx.ext4.journal-preflight=1 boot is a strictly read-only shadow-replay classifier, but it cannot prove actual replay writes/barriers, classic orphan recovery, or later RW runtime construction. It does not remove the need for safe writable media.
The VF2 MMC barrier may report success without a hardware flush. sync success alone is never persistence proof; a completed physical reset and same-disk RO verification remain mandatory.
Keep clone/compiler silence bounded and preserve the complete serial log. Do not replace the required full clone with --depth, tmpfs, or a simpler command.
